How Do These Weights Affect The Score?

Capital growth: Rewards LGAs with higher annualised changes in median sale prices over five years.

Rental yield: Rewards higher indicative gross rental yields (annualised median new-bond rent divided by median sale price).

Affordability: Rewards lower median sale prices, independently of your budget filter.

Each factor is ranked from 0–100 against eligible NSW LGAs. The weights are converted to proportions of their total: for example, 5 growth + 5 yield + 0 affordability makes growth and yield count 50% each. A zero weight excludes a factor; if all are zero, no score is produced. Scores describe historical patterns, not predicted returns.

A score out of 100 is a relative comparison, not a 100% chance of profit. Areas with missing data for selected factors are not scored.

What Does “5-Year Median CAGR” Mean?

Compound annual growth rate (CAGR) is the constant yearly rate that would take an LGA's published median sale price from its March 2021 quarter value to its March 2026 quarter value. Formula: (2026 median ÷ 2021 median)1/5 − 1, multiplied by 100. For example, $500,000 to $700,000 over five years is about 7.0% per year. It describes historical median changes, not a property's realised return or a prediction; changes in properties sold can influence the medians.

Data & Definitions

Expand a topic to read more
Data Sources & Periods

Property: NSW Department of Communities and Justice Rent and Sales Reports, quarterly LGA tables, supplied for this project. The common sales/rent period is January–March 2026; separate price/rent charts may extend into 2026 where available. Geography and Census: ABS ASGS 2021 Local Government Areas and ABS 2021 Census General Community Profile, loaded from the official ABS ArcGIS service.

Scoring Methodology & 5-Year CAGR

Scoring: weighted average of (i) percentile rank of five-year annualised change in median sale price, (ii) percentile of area-level indicative gross rental yield and (iii) reversed percentile of median price. Scores are calculated before budget filtering, based on areas with all positively weighted indicators observed. They describe relative historical observations, not future performance.

Five-year CAGR: (median price in 2026 Q1 ÷ median price in 2021 Q1)1/5 − 1, expressed as a percentage. This is historical annualised change in area medians, not individual-property appreciation. Weights from 0 to 5 are normalised by their sum.

Limitations & Reproducibility

Interpret carefully: sale medians and newly lodged rent medians come from different properties. Strata/non-strata and house/unit classifications are proxies, not direct matches. The 2021 ABS demographic snapshot predates the 2026 Q1 property statistics; unmatched LGA names stay unassigned. Historical boundary changes, delayed sales notifications, missing/suppressed cells and changing transaction mix affect comparisons. Townhouse research is rental-only: no comparable DCJ townhouse-specific sale category is published, so no yield or score is calculated.

Reproducible R Shiny code and raw cleaned DCJ datasets are included in the companion project repository. The website is a browser-based interactive view of those published source data, not a server-hosted R Shiny instance.
